tagline.text: A 360-degree sunrise view of eastern Bohol from the ridge of the Binabaje Hills

location.label: Location
location.text: Binabaje Hills, Alicia, eastern Bohol (Barangay Mahayag or Cambaol depending on the source), about 110 km from Tagbilaran

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day (mainly sunrise or sunset)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (per person, based on a day trip from Tagbilaran by public transport and motorcycle taxi, including the entrance fee and meals)

children.text: Alicia Panoramic Park is a viewpoint park in the Binabaje Hills of Alicia, eastern Bohol, where a ridge of about 400 m covered in cogon grass offers 360-degree views of the countryside. The entrance fee is about ₱20, and the walking time varies greatly by source.
Alicia Panoramic Park (TAPP) is a viewpoint park in the municipality of Alicia, eastern Bohol, set on the ridge of the Binabaje Hills. The hills are about

above sea level and are covered in green cogon grass. The park is known for open 360-degree views; one visitor says you can see the Bohol countryside and as far as the dam at Ubay on a clear day, while another guide says you can see toward the Chocolate Hills and the Rajah Sikatuna Protected Landscape. Visitors also mention birdsong. The location differs by source, being given as Barangay Mahayag or Barangay Cambaol, and OpenStreetMap marks a point on the Mabini side, so check the entrance on a map app first.
Alicia is a small town about
110 km

east of Tagbilaran. It became independent on January 18, 1950 from Batuanan, formerly part of Mabini, and is named after Alicia Syquia, the wife of President Elpidio Quirino. It covers about 114.5 sq km in 15 barangays, had about 25,000 residents in 2024, and borders Ubay, Pilar, Mabini and Candijay. The mean daily maximum temperature is 28–31 ℃ and annual rainfall is reported at about 1,326 mm. A fiesta honoring its patron Saint Joachim is held on July 26, and the Alicia Bamboo Ensemble, a school orchestra at Katipunan Elementary School, is known for winning prizes in national competitions. The panoramic park is almost the only signature attraction of the town, so most travelers come combined with Candijay and Anda. The town center is the Poblacion, also called Calingganay (about 4,200 residents), and the next largest barangay is La Hacienda (about 3,800). It is a 3rd-class municipality by income with about 5,800 households. For a town of this size, do not expect banks, ATMs or large restaurants, and it is safer to prepare cash in Tagbilaran or Candijay beforehand. Elevation is about 84 m in town, with a lowest point of 3 m and a highest of about 400 m, so the Binabaje Hills area can be seen as the highest ground in the municipality. The mean daily minimum temperature is about 23–24 ℃, so it is hot by day and cooler on the ridge at night and at dawn.

Reported walking times vary widely. A June 2025 guide (VisMin) says it takes about 30–45 minutes to the summit after a motorcycle taxi ride to the park entrance, while a 2018 guide (Around Bohol) says about 2 hours from the foot of the hills and about 4 hours on foot from the town. One tour product allots about 5 hours to this stop. Either way, some sections are steep and the last stretch has no shade and is hot. Ropes and handrails are said to be installed on some steep sections. At the summit there is a rest shed, a campsite, a view deck and a toilet using stored rainwater. It can be a challenge for first-time trekkers, so allow plenty of fitness and time.

The geology is also a talking point. One blog explains that the "Alicia Schist" here is the oldest rock formation in Bohol, dating from roughly 146 to 66 million years ago. Such explanations come from a personal blog, so confirm the geological details with a local guide. The park is not yet a crowded place and is relatively quiet, but that also means few facilities and little guidance, so it is better to take care of your gear and transport plan yourself.

From the summit the countryside of eastern Bohol spreads out in every direction. Guides say you can see toward the Chocolate Hills and the Rajah Sikatuna Protected Landscape, and the sea on a clear day. On cloudy days the view is blocked, so choose a clear day. There is almost no shade on the ridge, so early morning or late afternoon is recommended. When you rest at the top, take shelter from the wind under the shed roof and drink plenty of water.

The VisMin guide recommends 5:30–7:00 a.m. for sunrise and 4:00–5:30 p.m. for sunset. If you want to climb before dawn, it is safer to stay in a nearby town the night before. We could not confirm the exact opening hours, so check locally.

blocks.title: Cogon-grass hills and the Alicia Schist

children.text: The cogon grass covering the ridge and the gentle curves are the signature of the landscape here. The hills are said to lie on the Alicia Schist formation, which is described as the oldest rock in Bohol.

The summit is said to have a rest shed, a campsite, a view deck and a toilet that uses stored rainwater. There is reportedly no store at the campsite, so buy snacks and water at the registration area beforehand.
One visitor wrote that the dam at Ubay could be seen from the summit. On a clear day, binoculars help.
Various birds are said to be seen along the ridge. Birdsong is loud in the early morning, so climb quietly.

Tour products combine Alicia Panoramic Park with Can-umantad Falls, the Cadapdapan rice terraces and Quinale Beach in Anda in one day. Use the same order if you go on your own. Such a tour requires at least moderate fitness, lasts 9–12 hours and is described as including a private air-conditioned vehicle, a driver-guide and local guides. Meals and tips are extra, and cancellation up to 24 hours before is refunded. Conditions differ by operator, so check before booking.
The town center has the modest look of a small town, with a plaza, market, town hall and church. It is convenient to buy snacks and water at the market before you climb.

The climb at dawn is dark, so check your flashlight and shoes. Sunrise time changes with the season, so check the forecast and sunrise time the day before and arrive 30 minutes early.
Leave Tagbilaran and see the Candijay terraces and waterfall first.
Move to Alicia town and find a motorcycle taxi.

After sunset, come down and arrange your transport in town.
The last public transport leaves early, so decide your way back in advance.

1 hour 20 minutes

30 minutes
by taxi or van.
From the Dao Integrated Bus Terminal in Tagbilaran, take a bus or van bound for Carmen, Ubay or Talibon and get off in Alicia town. The VisMin guide says it takes about
1.5–2 hours
and costs

It varies with road conditions and available vehicles, so allow extra time.

One guide says walking from town takes about
4 hours
, so most people use a motorcycle taxi.
A private vehicle can take you from town to the foot of the hills, which suits groups or people who want to avoid public transport.
There are one-day private tours combining Anda, Candijay and Alicia, and in this case about 5 hours is allotted to the park.
The ridge has little shade and the last stretch is open, so midday is hot. Sunrise or sunset times and the dry season are best for walking.
The summit is quite cold at night, so bring warm clothes if you camp. In the rainy season the trail is slippery and the view is blocked by rain.

In town, the daily high is 28–31 ℃ and the low about 23–24 ℃. The summit is windy, so it feels cooler at dawn and at dusk; bring a light jacket. Annual rainfall is about 1,326 mm with about 259 rainy days, which is fairly rainy for eastern Bohol.

Alicia town may have small guesthouses, but we could not confirm specific names. If you want to see the sunrise, it is easier to stay the night before in town or in nearby Candijay. There is a campsite at the summit, so camping is said to be possible.

The summit campsite has no store, so buy snacks and water beforehand at the registration area or in town. You can eat at the market and restaurants in town, and a warm soup and rice at a local eatery after the climb is a nice way to rest. For a sunrise or sunset climb that takes long, it is safer to carry at least 1 liter of water per person.
Bring water, snacks and a flashlight, and wear shoes with firm soles.
A guide is optional, but hire a local guide if you feel uneasy climbing alone.
If you want to climb for sunrise, stay in town the night before.
The summit is cold at night, so bring a jacket if you camp.
Carry your trash down and dispose of it only in designated places.
Agree on the return time with your motorcycle taxi driver when you arrive.
The last stretch has no shade, so bring a hat and sunscreen.
On cloudy days the view is blocked, so check the weather forecast.
It is hard to find banks or ATMs in town, so prepare cash before you leave. The entrance fee and motorcycle taxi fares are often paid in cash.
Walking times and trail conditions differ between sources, so it is risky to think of this as a short stroll. If it is your first time, climb with a guide during the day.
Some sections are steep, so hold the handrails and ropes and move slowly.
The soil is slippery after rain, so be careful with your shoes and steps.
The barangay and opening hours of the park differ between sources, so check the entrance on a map app.
When going up or down in the dark, bring a flashlight and a companion.
The information in this article reflects what could be verified as of 2026; check the latest announcements.
The park is relatively quiet with few facilities, so when you climb alone, tell someone your plans.
